detail: Reference solutions (float64, tol 1e-8) and the old production path.
verdict: CPU reference, 32 threads: full CV on unit-100k takes 4651 s, same answer as celer and the GPU working set. Fine at p = 1000 (29 s on pca1k), impractical in the unit basis.

detail: State-of-the-art CPU solver for p >> n; the yardstick for GPU work.
verdict: CPU reference, 32 threads: full CV takes 403 s on unit-100k and 2269 s on unit-800k (64 channels), with the same R2 and supports as the GPU working set.

detail: Lasso has to justify itself against Ridge on test R2 in the unit basis.
verdict: The R2 reference: unit-100k reliable R2 0.347 (0.352 raw) in 2 to 3 s on CPU; layer3 units 0.303; layer1 units 0.125. Lasso gets within 0.02 of it at about 300 units per channel, is 0.04 below at 100 and 0.14 below at 30. Keeping Ridge's top 1000 weights and refitting gives 0.355.

detail: Old runs used unscaled PCA columns (std 1 to 48); suspected cause of slow, non-converging fits.
verdict: Keep z-scoring as the default in the unit basis. Layer4 units: Lasso 0.326 z-scored vs 0.316 raw, Ridge 0.347 vs 0.352. Layer1 units: z-scoring helps both (Lasso 0.033 vs 0.003, Ridge 0.125 vs 0.076). Only on PCA features does it hurt.

detail: Old use ran 500 tiny fits one at a time and was far slower than CPU.
verdict: No results yet

idea: Batched FISTA over targets x alphas
detail: Two big matmuls per iteration, restart, per-problem gap stopping, float32 vs float64.
verdict: Dropped as the unit-basis solver; kept only for small p. On unit-100k one path takes 553 s on H200 (371 s with screening) and over half the problems still miss gap 1e-4, against 39 s for the working set. Cause: real unit features are badly conditioned for a global step size. Still the fastest at p = 1000 (pca1k CV in 2.4 s).

detail: The plain deep-learning optimizer route; only option when X does not fit on the GPU.
verdict: Dropped as a sparse method. Their higher R2 (0.36) comes from being dense: read at the same number of nonzeros, prox-SGD and prox-Adam lose 0.04 to 0.15 R2 against relaxed exact Lasso for k up to 100, and still trail by 0.01 to 0.03 after a ridge refit. Minibatch variant remains the fallback if X cannot fit on a GPU.

idea: w = u*v reparametrization with weight decay
detail: Smooth objective whose minima match the Lasso; exact-zero seeking without a prox step.
verdict: Kept as the reference answer only: 1000 Adam epochs plus a final prox step reproduce exact Lasso on unit-100k (reliable R2 0.326, median 121.5 nonzeros vs 120.5), at 219 s against 11.5 s for the working set. Tracks exact Lasso at every sparsity level, never beats it.

detail: Simplest gradient variant; sparsity only after post-hoc thresholding.
verdict: Dropped: denser (955 nonzeros) and slower (185 s) than exact Lasso for 0.007 more R2, and no advantage at matched sparsity.

idea: GPU-screened working set, small Gram subproblems
detail: GPU computes X'R for all targets; each problem is solved on a few hundred features. Expected front-runner.
verdict: The solver we keep. Full CV on H200: unit-100k in 11.5 s (6.5 s in a warm process; 13.7 s on A100), unit-800k with 64 channels in 20 s, same R2 and supports as celer (403 s and 2269 s on 32 CPU threads) and sklearn CD (4651 s). Time is almost flat in the number of features: a full 384-channel path takes 14 to 27 s for 1e4 to 1e6 synthetic features. CV early stopping gave 3 to 25x with identical selections.

detail: Better dual points for earlier stopping and tighter screening, as in celer.
verdict: Kept. Anderson extrapolation in the inner coordinate-descent kernel gives 2 to 4x (16.4 s -> 4.2 s on a small tight-tolerance test).

idea: Batch the CV folds into one solve
detail: Fold masks as row weights or Gram downdates so all 6 fits share work.
verdict: Kept, on by default. Solving the folds as row-masked problems in one batch is 4x faster on a synthetic tier and removed the 5x A100 slowdown (the old rule ran folds one after another on 80 GB cards): unit-100k CV 171 s -> 13.7 s on A100.

idea: Woodbury ADMM with one shared n x n Cholesky
detail: One factorization serves every target and alpha; fast low-accuracy solutions.
verdict: Dropped. It wins only at small p and loose tolerance, which batched FISTA already covers. unit-100k path to gap 1e-4: 51 s vs 39 s for the working set on H200; on A100 it did not reach 1e-4 in 139 s. Each iteration costs two full matrix products, against about one per alpha for the working set.

detail: Exploits second-order sparsity when active sets are small; optional stretch.
verdict: Not built and not planned: it would only help in the dense tail of the path, and CV early stopping removed most of that cost.

idea: Relaxed Lasso: ridge refit on the Lasso support
detail: Removes the shrinkage bias of Lasso weights while keeping the same selected units.
verdict: Helps only for very sparse models. Read at a fixed number of units it lifts R2 a lot (unit-100k, 10 units: 0.125 -> 0.221; 30 units: 0.220 -> 0.282), confirmed by two sessions, for about 3.4 s extra. At the CV-chosen alpha it changes nothing: 0.326 with or without refit in the harness, and 0.313 with a sparser model (158 vs 238 units on reliable channels) in the solver's own CV. So the Lasso-vs-Ridge gap is lost features, not shrinkage. The penalty must be chosen by CV over the whole select-then-refit procedure; a fixed small penalty is unstable and is dropped.

detail: Pick the sparsest model within one SE of the best CV error instead of the best one.
verdict: unit-100k: 0.294 with 82 units per reliable channel, against 0.326 with 252 for the min-error rule: 3x sparser for 0.03 R2, slightly more stable across folds (Jaccard 0.21 vs 0.15), and 88% of picks are top-1% correlated units. On layer1 it selects the empty model. Report both rules.

detail: A little L2 can stabilize supports among correlated units.
verdict: Kept as an option, not sparser. unit-100k 0.328 (Lasso 0.326) with 280 vs 238 units on reliable channels; layer1 0.059 vs 0.033. Fold stability unchanged (0.156 vs 0.148).

detail: Train directly under a fixed number of nonzeros per channel.
verdict: Dropped: loses 0.03 to 0.07 R2 against relaxed Lasso at 10 to 100 nonzeros, and still 0.006 to 0.047 after a ridge refit. The Adam version is unstable.

idea: Gaussian point readout (dualneuron): one position x channel weights
detail: Reproduce the dualneuron readout on our frozen features, faithful (Poisson) and like-for-like (MSE, linear).
verdict: Dropped as a sparse alternative. unit-100k reliable R2 0.265 faithful and 0.305 for the best (linear) variant, 5-member ensembles, against Ridge 0.347 and Lasso 0.326; layer3 0.26 to 0.28 against Ridge 0.303. Its L1 under Adam never produces zeros; with a proximal step it keeps 135 to 166 channels (540 to 660 units), still less sparse than Lasso.

idea: Low-rank space x feature readout by gradient descent (rank 1 to 3)
detail: W = spatial mask (H x W) times feature vector (C), proximal L1 on both factors.
verdict: Round 2 (5 splits, single fit against single fit): not better than Ridge on layer4 (+0.006 R2, SE 0.004; the earlier +0.02 compared a 5-member ensemble with one Ridge fit), better on layer3 (+0.030 to +0.036, 5 of 5 splits). Superseded by nuclear-norm regression, which gains about twice as much and needs no seeds. Rank-1 spatial mask is stable on layer4 (|cos| 0.96 across seeds, 0.78 across disjoint halves) but not on layer3 (0.64 across seeds alone); the feature vector is not reproducible across halves (0.40, 0.34). Still fast (21 s full protocol at 800k units) but 10k to 20k nonzero units.

idea: Space x feature readout by alternating Lasso solves
detail: Each factor is an exact Lasso given the other; sparsity in feature channels rather than units.
verdict: Matches Lasso R2 on layer4 (0.315 to 0.326 ensemble) with only 59 to 70 distinct feature channels per neuron, but 400 to 1,100 units. Slow (4 to 7 min) and unstable at rank 2 to 3 on layer3. Worth a follow-up only if the question is which feature channels matter.

idea: Is the Lasso solution spatially point-like?
detail: Spatial concentration of each channel's selected units.
verdict: No. Lasso spreads over 45 of 49 positions on layer4; the best position holds 12% of the weight and the best 2x2 window 32%, about twice chance. All reliable channels share the same central receptive-field region.

detail: Do different subsets of the training images select the same units?
verdict: The main open problem. On unit-100k, two Lasso fits on disjoint halves of the images share only 1 to 2% of their selected units (Jaccard 0.007 to 0.022); the five CV folds, which share 80% of their data, share 15 to 26%. Counting feature maps instead of single units helps little (halves 0.07 to 0.13). Ridge's top-100 units are just as unstable (0.03). The 1-SE rule is somewhat more stable and 88% of its picks are among the top 1% most correlated units. With 822 images the selected units are not identifiable for any method tested. Round 2 confirms this with weights instead of supports: across disjoint halves the Lasso weight cosine is 0.02 (Ridge 0.17, nuclear norm 0.27, rank-1 low-rank 0.34). Predictions are far more stable than parameters for every model (test-prediction correlation 0.68 to 0.79).

idea: Nuclear-norm (convex low-rank) readout, rank chosen by CV
detail: Per channel, penalize the nuclear norm of the feature x position weight matrix; FISTA with singular-value thresholding.
verdict: Best single model measured so far. unit-100k 0.384 against Ridge 0.358 (mean of 5 splits; +0.026, SE 0.004, better on 5 of 5); layer3 with clipped test columns 0.389 against 0.324 (+0.066, 5 of 5). Chooses rank about 4. Dense in units, so it does not serve the sparsity goal by itself; its leading spatial factor is stable across disjoint halves (|cos| 0.88, 0.84), its feature factor is not (0.34, 0.40). Solver is unoptimized: about 7 min per split on layer4, 24 min on layer3; not yet run at 800k.

detail: Combine the low-rank structure that predicts best with unit-level sparsity.
verdict: Proposed by the factorized-readout session after round 2; needs a faster nuclear-norm solver first.

idea: Nonnegative Lasso (positive=True) in the working-set solver
detail: One-sided soft threshold and one-sided duality gap in torch_ws; weights constrained to be >= 0.
verdict: Reviewed and tested, merge pending. On unit-100k the nonnegative fit loses almost no R2 (0.322 against 0.326), uses 18% fewer nonzeros (106 against 129 per channel) and runs 1.7x faster (3.9 s against 6.6 s, H200). Matches sklearn Lasso(positive=True) to 1e-10 in objective. Poor on PCA and synthetic tiers, where true weights are signed. Not yet combinable with elastic net or relaxed refit; the harness gap check is two-sided and needs a positive-aware version.

idea: Layer3 test-set outliers: clip test columns to training range
detail: Sparse layer3 units z-scored on training rows reach values of several thousand on test images.
verdict: Per-unit Lasso and Ridge blow up on some splits (Lasso test R2 below -100 on two of five); clipping to the training range fixes it and raises Lasso from 0.221 to 0.248 on the tier's own split. The layer3 harness rows should be rebuilt with clipping.
